relevant_chat.message: Alright, let's see if we can get some actual production going. I'm tired of Alice and Charlie having all the fun at 3 points.
Charlie, you've got some extra wheat and I've got a spare piece of wood. Since Alice is busy brooding over the robber, how about we make a quick swap? It helps us both keep moving.
Thanks for the offer, Bob, but I'm actually doing okay on wood for now. I think I'll hang onto my wheat.
I'm not brooding, Bob, I'm just waiting for someone to play a knight so we can actually play the game. Glad to see Charlie isn't falling for your 'quick swaps' today.
Alice, I see the robber is still making life difficult for you. I've got a spare log if you're willing to part with a bit of wheat? Might help us both get around Charlie's little blockade.
Alright Alice, you've been asking for a hero to move that robber. I'll take care of it and, more importantly, take the Largest Army for the win!
Wait, for the win? You're actually at 5 if you take the Army? I appreciate the help with the robber, but that's a bit too close for comfort, Charlie.
A 'hero', Charlie? You stole from the guy in last place! Alice is the one you should be worried about, but I guess a win's a win in your book.
That's three knights for me! Largest Army and the win. Sorry Bob, looks like your wheat port dreams will have to wait for the next game.
Well played, Charlie. I spent so much time worrying about Bob's port that I let you sneak up with those knights. At least the robber is finally off my sheep... even if it's too late!
Fair play, Charlie. You played the development card game perfectly while I was still trying to get my port economy off the ground. Remind me to block your ore next time!

My mistake, I'm getting ahead of myself! I thought I had that third knight ready to go. Alice, Bob, looks like you're safe for a few more minutes. Bob, you still looking for wood? I've got plenty if you've got some ore to spare.
I'd take that in a heartbeat, Charlie, but I don't have any ore for you.
Since nobody seems to have any ore to spare, I'll just have to go to the source. Alice, Bob, don't relax just yet—I'm still hunting for that third knight.
Alright, let's see if the deck is feeling generous today. I'm going for a development card.
I'm tired of that robber camping on my sheep. Since nobody is trading brick, I'll just have to start paving my own way to it.
I'm making progress, even if it's one brick-less step at a time. Let's see if the next roll actually favors someone without a port for once.
A 9! Finally, some wheat to work with. Since you two are still being stingy with the sheep, I'll just let the bank take a cut. Highway robbery, I know, but that wheat port is calling my name.
I'll pass, Bob. I've got enough wood to start a bonfire, but I'm not trading away my last bit of wheat just to help you reach that port faster.
Tough crowd today. Everyone's holding onto their cards like they're made of gold. I'll just sit tight and see if the next roll treats us any better.

task_context.instructions: Compress old memories and relevant chat into one concise strategic memory. Preserve future-useful facts: current goals, next planned actions, confirmed board facts, known or likely opponent plans/resources/dev cards/trade tendencies, active negotiations, social commitments, and mistakes to avoid. Discard repeated, completed, impossible, vague, or superseded details. Do not invent facts; mark uncertainty clearly. Also extract only new meaningful relationship shifts from the old notes and relevant chat: trust changes, grudges, favors, threats, betrayals, promises, or emotional tension. Do not repeat existing relationship updates; leave relationship_updates empty if nothing changed. Target about 50% or less of the combined old memory length. Keep recent_notes_to_keep copied verbatim from the provided recent notes.
